To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
learning analytics dashboards are not designed and evaluated based on theories of learning and that the design of such dashboards can benefit from the use of theories of learning.

learning analytics dashboards are not being designed and evaluated in line with the theoretical foundation of learning sciences and that learners are not always positively affected by the use of comparison with peers as a reference frame for contextualizing learning analytics dashboards.

the theoretical foundation of learning analytics dash- boards should be clearly defined, that learners' privacy concerns should be addressed, and that the use of comparison with peers should be carefully considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how learning sciences can contribute to the development and evaluation of learning dashboards, with the purpose of informing the development of learning analytics interventions in general, and learning dashboards in particular.
the design and evaluation processes of learning analytics dashbots, and the role that learning sciences should play in these processes.
how learning analytics interventions, in this case learning dashboards, can be informed by learning sciences to better support learners and teachers in online learning environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the design of learning analytics dash- boards for learners should be based on learning science theories, and the effectiveness of such interventions should be assessed in the context of the theoretical foundations used in their design.
the learning sciences can inform the design of learning analytics dash-boards and their evaluation.
the current state of the practice of learning analytics is not ready to support learners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning analytics dashboards should be evaluated with respect to their educational purpose.

the design of dashboards for learners should be informed by learning sciences theories and models, and that evaluation of dashboards should consider the extent to which learners understand the concepts used to inform the design of the dashboards.

learning analytics dashboards should not only be evaluated for their technical quality, but that they should also be evaluated from the perspective of the educational theory that informed their design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning analytics dashboards should not be designed and evaluated in isolation from the theories and models that underlie their design.
learning analytics dashboards should be designed and evaluated in a manner that reflects the theories and models that inform their design, and that learners should be consulted in the design process.
, in order to be effective, learning analytics interventions should be informed by learning theories and models.
